INTEGRATED SCIENCE — MOCK EXAM #19
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Milk souring
   D. Iron rusting

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Integrated Science? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Integrated Science.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Integrated Science.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Integrated Science.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Integrated Science.

3. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Only water vapour

4. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 50 °C

5. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. newton (N)
   B. joule (J)
   C. watt (W)
   D. pascal (Pa)

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Human Excretory System 18 4.0 Force and Energy 4.1 Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magn? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Human Excretory System 18 4.0 Force and Energy 4.1 Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magn.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Human Excretory System 18 4.0 Force and Energy 4.1 Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magn.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Human Excretory System 18 4.0 Force and Energy 4.1 Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magn.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Human Excretory System 18 4.0 Force and Energy 4.1 Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magn.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Acids, Bases and Indicators? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Acids, Bases and Indicators.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Acids, Bases and Indicators.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Acids, Bases and Indicators.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Acids, Bases and Indicators.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Magnetism? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Magnetism.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Magnetism.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Magnetism.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Magnetism.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Laboratory Safety? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Laboratory Safety.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Laboratory Safety.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Laboratory Safety.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Laboratory Safety.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Laboratory apparatus and instruments? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Laboratory apparatus and instruments.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Laboratory apparatus and instruments.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Laboratory apparatus and instruments.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Laboratory apparatus and instruments.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Human Excretory System? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Human Excretory System.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Human Excretory System.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Human Excretory System.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Human Excretory System.

12. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Water always increases oxygen

13. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Producers
   D. Primary consumers only

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Electrical Energy? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Electrical Energy.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Electrical Energy.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Electrical Energy.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Electrical Energy.

15. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magnetism 16 Total Number of Lessons 150 Note: The sugg? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magnetism 16 Total Number of Lessons 150 Note: The sugg.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magnetism 16 Total Number of Lessons 150 Note: The sugg.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magnetism 16 Total Number of Lessons 150 Note: The sugg.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magnetism 16 Total Number of Lessons 150 Note: The sugg.

17. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Burning crop residue every week

18. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. Heating until a solid melts

19. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. A mixture of two liquids

20. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Human Reproductive System? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Human Reproductive System.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Human Reproductive System.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Human Reproductive System.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Human Reproductive System.

21. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Mixtures? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Mixtures.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Mixtures.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Mixtures.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Mixtures.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
22. In three clear sentences, explain Human Excretory System 18 4.0 Force and Energy 4.1 Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magn and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Human Excretory System and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Electrical Energy 18 4.2 Magnetism 16 Total Number of Lessons 150 Note: The sugg and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

25. In three clear sentences, explain Electrical Energy and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

26. In three clear sentences, explain Magnetism and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

27. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Integrated Science and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

28. In three clear sentences, explain Laboratory Safety and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

29. In three clear sentences, explain Laboratory apparatus and instruments and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
